sn20.7:1.2: Probably the people known in Sanskrit as the Daśārṇa of the western Vindhya mountains. | The _mudiṅga_ is a doubled-headed drum known today as _mridangam_, which is still widely used in southern India. It is named for the paste (“mud”) applied to one of the heads that gives it its distinctive snare tone. The head is attached with a wooden rim that is tightened with leather straps.
sn20.7:1.4: Puskara is another kind of drum, identified with the mudinga
